headline: FPL and NEER both grow as Dominion deal advances
summary_short: NextEra Energy's Q2 FY2026 GAAP net income attributable to the company rose 55.0% y/y to $3.144 billion ($1.50 diluted EPS), while adjusted EPS of $1.15 grew 9.5% y/y as FPL grew regulatory capital employed ~9.3% y/y and NextEra Energy Resources added 3.6 GW to its backlog.
summary_long: GAAP EPS growth (+53.1% y/y) outpaces adjusted EPS growth (+9.5% y/y to $1.15) because GAAP includes favorable hedge and nuclear-fund mark-to-market swings versus unfavorable ones a year ago. FPL net income rose to $1.412B (+10.7% y/y) on disciplined capital investment and ~9.3% y/y regulatory capital employed growth. NEER's adjusted net income rose to $1.291B (+18.3% y/y) on strong renewables/storage origination (3.6 GW added, backlog ~35.1 GW). Cash rose to $2.866B from $2.812B at year-end; long-term debt rose to $98.79B from $89.56B. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance held at $3.92-$4.02, targeting the high end; 8%+ EPS CAGR through 2032 reaffirmed. The Dominion Energy combination advanced with merger filings at FERC, NRC and three states; the SEC registration statement went effective July 23.
